[[lem-borel-product-of-second-countable-spaces|Borel measurability on finite products of the Lie group]]

[F7] The Lie group is second-countable, so its finite-product Borel sigma-algebra equals the product sigma-algebra; continuous face-holonomy, gauge-action, and density maps are measurable for these structures. [[def-qftx-su2-wilson-plaquette-measure|Explicit SU(2) coordinates, round measure, plaquette weight, and trace convention]]

[F1] [[def-qftx-su2-wilson-plaquette-measure]]: $SU(2)$ is the matrix set $\{U:U^*U=I_2,\det U=1\}$, $\tau(U)=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}_2(U)=x_0$, and $\mu_2$ is the pushforward of normalized round surface measure $\sigma_3$ on $S^3$; explicitly, for every Borel $A\subseteq SU(2)$, $\mu_2(A)=\sigma_3(\{x\in S^3:U(x)\in A\})$. The same definition states the spherical-coordinate density that step 1.2 establishes locally before using.

[[lem-equivariant-symbol-chern-character-pushforward]]

[L3] The trace-weighted ordinary compact-symbol pushforward is the cotangent integral of its relative Chern character times $\operatorname{Td}(TF_{\mathbb C})$, with precisely the stated orientation. It respects localized quotients and retains the full normal characteristic denominator. [[lem-equivariant-symbol-chern-character-pushforward]]

[F3] Representative functions of a compact group, meaning finite sums of matrix coefficients of finite-dimensional continuous representations, are uniformly dense in its continuous functions. [[thm-uniform-peter-weyl-density]]
[[lem-equivariant-controlled-symbol-realization]]

[F2] The analytic index of elliptic symbols is invariant under stabilized symbol homotopy, quantization and Sobolev order reduction. Invariant open symbols have representatives equal to an isomorphism plus a kernel supported in $C\times C$ for invariant compact $C$ inside the open set; restriction/extension identifies kernel and adjoint kernel in any compactification, proving excision. These assertions hold for compact acting groups, including disconnected groups. [[lem-equivariant-controlled-symbol-realization]]

[F2] Controlled realization gives an additive representation-valued index on compact-support symbol classes, independent of compactification by excision, invariant under stabilized symbol homotopy and equivariant diffeomorphism, and compatible with group restriction and coefficient representations. On compact manifolds it is the kernel-minus-adjoint-kernel of an elliptic realization. No Bott normalization or embedding-index equality is assumed. [[lem-equivariant-controlled-symbol-realization]]

[F2] The compact symbol index is invariant under stabilized symbol homotopy, equals the Fredholm kernel difference of a realization, is compatible with coefficient representations, and is independent of compactification for controlled compact-support representatives. [[lem-equivariant-controlled-symbol-realization]]

[F2] Compact-symbol realization supplies a representation-valued analytic index respecting continuous symbol homotopy, elementary stabilization, block sums, group restriction, coefficients and equivariant diffeomorphisms. Its two-cutoff construction identifies kernel and adjoint kernel across two supplied compact ambient embeddings of an invariant open set. For a first-order elliptic complex it proves the matrix-symbol Hodge/cohomology identification. [[lem-equivariant-controlled-symbol-realization]]
[[lem-equivariant-symbol-index-comparison]]

[L1] Compact-symbol analytic realization identifies the complex's index with $a_{T,M}(\sigma)$. Analytic Gysin compatibility holds for a real equivariant embedding. On a base fixed by $g$, evaluation is the eigenvalue-weighted ordinary topological pushforward. The full analytic calculus, controlled excision, positive-order associated product and orthogonal Bott normalization are proved in its prerequisite chain. [[lem-equivariant-symbol-index-comparison]]

[F3] Ordinary bundle clutching over $Y\times S^2$ can be normalized; a circle clutching family can be uniformly approximated by a finite Laurent family, negative powers cleared, and the polynomial family stabilized by explicit block matrices to a linear one. The latter splits into its inside and outside spectral subbundles. The resulting inverse to product with $1,\beta$ is given by the minus spectral subbundle and the Laurent shift.
